editorial:
Imagine starting your marriage with a total disaster. That is exactly what happens to Siniša and Svetlana. They think they are heading to Spain for a dreamy honeymoon, but a travel agency screw-up lands them on the coast of Montenegro instead. It is a funny, relatable start to a story about a couple just trying to get their lives together in Belgrade. The vibe is lighthearted and captures that feeling of everything going wrong at once, making you root for them even when they make questionable choices.

What really makes this work is the absurd plot. To get a government apartment, the couple decides to fake a divorce because single mothers get priority. The acting is natural, and the pacing keeps you interested as their lie gets more complicated. While some parts feel a bit dated, the humor still hits home.
endingExplained: The couple spends the whole movie pretending to be separated to trick the housing board. In the end, the stress of the lie and the fake divorce actually puts a real strain on their relationship. However, they eventually realize that their love is stronger than their desire for a free apartment. They drop the act, reconcile their marriage, and decide that being together is more important than gaming the system to get a place to live.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quirky romantic comedies and stories about couples fighting the system.
